memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus and rheumatoid arthritis.
He reports mild polyuria and occasional joint stiffness in the mornings. On exam, blood pressure 138/82, pulse 78, BMI 22. Lung fields clear, no wheeze. Hands show mild synovitis of MCP joints, no deformities. Foot pulses palpable.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Metformin 500 mg BD
Glimepiride 1 mg OD before breakfast
Sitagliptin 100 mg OD
Empagliflozin 10 mg OD
Methotrexate 10 mg once weekly
Folic acid 5 mg once weekly
Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg OD
Prednisolone 5 mg OD

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
HbA1c 7.8%
Fasting plasma glucose 156 mg/dL
Urine albumin-creatinine ratio 22 mg/g
ESR 28 mm/hr
CRP 6 mg/L
Rheumatoid factor 28 IU/mL (positive)
Anti-CCP 45 U/mL (borderline)
ALT 22 U/L, AST 20 U/L, ALP 78 U/L, GGT 30 U/L
Dilated fundus exam: mild microaneurysms, no macular edema.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow-up appointment booked for 2025-07-01 at 10:00 AM with Dr Suresh Menon (D05) in Pulmonology clinic.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Stable type 2 diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis.
He notes improved energy, occasional knee pain after walking. Exam: BP 132/80, pulse 76, lungs clear. Joint exam: mild tenderness in wrists, no swelling. Spirometry: FEV1 2.10 L (78% predicted), FVC 2.55 L (80% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.82; change since baseline +0.05 L. ACT score 22 (well controlled). Technique checked: correct.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Metformin 500 mg BD (continue)
Glimepiride 1 mg OD (continue)
Sitagliptin 100 mg OD (continue)
Empagliflozin 10 mg OD (continue)
Methotrexate 10 mg once weekly (continue)
Folic acid 5 mg once weekly (continue)
Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg OD (continue)
Prednisolone 5 mg OD (reduce to 2.5 mg OD)

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Spirometry performed: FEV1 2.10 L (78% predicted), FVC 2.55 L (80% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.82. No bronchodilator response. Interpretation: normal spirometry for age.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have been having more pain and swelling in my fingers and feet over the past month, especially in the mornings. It hurts to type lectures and I feel tired.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Rheumatoid arthritis flare.
He describes increased joint pain, morning stiffness >45 minutes, fatigue. Exam: BP 136/84, pulse 80. Symmetric swelling and tenderness of MCP and PIP joints of both hands, mild synovitis of MTP joints. Lung clear.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Methotrexate increased to 15 mg once weekly
Folic acid 5 mg once weekly (continue)
Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg OD (continue)
Prednisolone increased to 10 mg OD for 2 weeks then taper to 5 mg OD
Other diabetes medications unchanged.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
ESR 48 mm/hr
CRP 12 mg/L
Rheumatoid factor 32 IU/mL
Anti-CCP 52 U/mL
ALT 24 U/L, AST 22 U/L, ALP 80 U/L, GGT 32 U/L

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Referral to Rheumatology, Dr Niranjan Patel, for assessment of aggressive rheumatoid arthritis and consideration of biologic therapy.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Rheumatology review: patient continues methotrexate 15 mg weekly, hydroxychloroquine, low-dose prednisolone. Added sulfasalazine 500 mg BD. Advised to continue current diabetes regimen. Follow-up in 8 weeks.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Type 2 diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis, stable on updated regimen.
He reports less joint swelling, morning stiffness 20 minutes, good glycaemic control. Exam: BP 130/78, pulse 76, lungs clear. Joints: mild tenderness, no effusion. Spirometry: FEV1 2.12 L (79% predicted), FVC 2.58 L (81% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.82; change +0.02 L since last. ACT score 23 (well controlled). Technique checked: correct.
